ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the graph, in the Cartesian coordinate system $xOy$, we have $OA=OB$ and $\angle AOB=90^\circ$. A line parallel to the $x$-axis is drawn through point B, and it intersects with the line passing through point A, which is $y=-x+b$, at point C. Given that the coordinates of point A are (2, 1), what is the degree measure of $\angle ACB$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Let the line intersect the y-axis at point E, as shown in the figure:\\
$\therefore OD=OE$,\\
$\therefore \angle OEC=\angle ODC=45^\circ$,\\
Also, since $BC\parallel OD$,\\
$\therefore \angle BCA+\angle CDO=180^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle BCA=135^\circ$,\\
Therefore, the measure of $\angle ACB$ is $\boxed{135^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a rectangular coordinate system xOy. Point A is located in the first quadrant and on the obliquely downward line y=-x+b; point B is located to the upper left of O; a horizontal line is drawn through B, intersecting the oblique line at C, and C is to the right of B and near the upper left of A. In the figure, OA and OB are marked as equal, and the included angle is 90°, which is consistent with B being the position of A rotated counterclockwise 90° around O. Reasoning: It is known that A=(2,1). Vector OA=(2,1); rotating it counterclockwise 90° gives (-1,2), so according to the direction in the figure take B=(-1,2). The line y=-x+b passes through A, so 1=-2+b, giving b=3, and the line is y=-x+3. The horizontal line through B is y=2. When it intersects y=-x+3, there is 2=-x+3, giving x=1, so C=(1,2). At point C, vector CA=A-C=(2,1)-(1,2)=(1,-1), vector CB=B-C=(-1,2)-(1,2)=(-2,0). The dot product CA·CB=1·(-2)+(-1)·0=-2, |CA|=sqrt(2), |CB|=2, so cos∠ACB=-2/(2sqrt(2))=-1/sqrt(2). Therefore ∠ACB=135°.
